notes: Hand-written bios for satellites that work well with Downlink Desk. Facts from each team's site, SatNOGS DB and Gunter's Space Page; checked October 2026.

satellites.name: GRBBeta
satellites.bio: Tests a small gamma-ray detector and electronics for CAMELOT, a planned constellation for spotting gamma-ray bursts. Successor to GRBAlpha, which re-entered in 2025. Carries UHF and VHF beacons, a CW beacon and an amateur digipeater. Launched on Ariane 6's first flight.

satellites.name: CroCube
satellites.bio: Croatia's first satellite, partly crowdfunded. A single-unit CubeSat built to grow Croatian space and STEM skills, it has sent back camera images of its home country.

satellites.name: Foresail-1p
satellites.bio: A second attempt after the original Foresail-1 failed. Carries a particle telescope for studying space radiation and a plasma brake: a charged tether that drags against the ionosphere to lower the orbit, a possible cheap way to clear dead satellites.

satellites.name: CatSat
satellites.bio: A student-built satellite testing an inflatable antenna, studying charged particles in the upper atmosphere and photographing Earth.

satellites.name: CubeBel-2
satellites.bio: Also called BSUSat-2. A teaching and research platform built by students and young scientists, with two multispectral Earth-observation cameras and an amateur radio digipeater. Its beacon is one of the richest on SatNOGS, with dozens of decoded fields.

satellites.name: Sharjahsat-1
satellites.bio: A University of Sharjah CubeSat carrying an improved X-ray detector for observing bright X-ray sources in the sky. Heard often by volunteer stations.

satellites.name: UWE-4
satellites.bio: A veteran in orbit since 2018. Became the first 1U CubeSat to show it could steer its own orbit, using tiny electric thrusters. Still transmitting years after launch.
